themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens spiked to 3 reports this week, a 700% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 0.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.42), signaling a potential escalation in open drug use or dealing in the neighborhood.
evidence: 3 drug activity complaints filed this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
700% spike with z-score of 5.42, indicating statistically significant deviation
Aligns with community board's repeated requests for enhanced park safety and security staff
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners in high-complaint areas (Prospect Park perimeter, commercial strips) about visible drug activity and safety concerns
Investigate whether NYPD enforcement response has changed or whether this is new street-level activity; check arrest records and precinct data

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints exploded this week to 3 reports, a 2300% increase from the 8-week baseline average of 0.1 weekly complaints (z-score: 8.69, highest statistical severity in district), suggesting rapid expansion of dining sheds or ongoing code violations.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase)
Highest z-score spike in district data at 8.69, indicating most anomalous deviation
Timing coincides with spring weather and potential removal of winter shed restrictions
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify which blocks are experiencing issues; interview affected residents about noise, blocking, or sanitation problems
Check Department of Health inspection records for recent violations at outdoor dining venues; investigate whether post-pandemic shed removals are incomplete

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Safety Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street sign complaints surged last week to 5 reports, a 1233% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 0.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.65), indicating potential weather damage or maintenance backlog creating public safety risks.
evidence: 5 dangling street sign complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1233% increase)
Z-score of 6.65 indicates highly anomalous spike
Likely triggered by recent weather events (winter storms, high winds) affecting signage across district
reporting_angles: Document locations of dangling signs with photos; assess public safety risk (pedestrian/vehicle injury potential)
Contact Department of Transportation to understand repair timeline and whether winter weather created maintenance backlog

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals and Wildlife Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 7 last week and animal-in-park complaints spiked to 5 two weeks ago (460% and 567% increases respectively from baseline), suggesting environmental or sanitation degradation or seasonal wildlife movement into residential areas.
evidence: 7 dead animal complaints last week vs. 1.2 weekly average (460% increase, z-score: 4.8)
5 animal-in-park complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% increase, z-score: 6.43)
Convergence of two wildlife-related spikes suggests broader environmental or sanitation issue
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about wildlife management in Prospect Park and other district parks; assess whether animal populations are increasing or food waste is attracting wildlife
Investigate dead animal disposal protocols and whether sanitation pickup issues are creating accumulation

themes_detail.label: Building Violations and Code Enforcement
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints surged to 9 two weeks ago, a 500% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 1.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.74), coinciding with 1,199 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (727 alterations), indicating possible code violations or illegal conversions amid active construction.
evidence: 9 building/use complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 4.74)
1,199 DOB permits filed in last 90 days, with 727 alterations suggesting heavy renovation activity
Active ULURP applications (46 Nelson Street rezoning in public review) indicate ongoing development pressure
reporting_angles: Cross-reference building complaints with DOB permit data to identify problem properties; investigate whether unlicensed contractors or illegal conversions (basement apartments, commercial-to-residential) are driving violations
Interview Department of Housing Preservation and Development about enforcement capacity; assess whether inspection backlogs are delaying violation remediation
